selection.name: C07 — OpenLIT
selection.role: Provisional sole choice for persistent local OTLP storage and inspection of agent and LLM calls. Its documented Claude Code and Codex instrumentation most directly covers the named users. This is a capability-and-install-fit judgment, not a claim of measured performance superiority.
selection.install_command:
git clone https://github.com/openlit/openlit.git
cd openlit
docker compose up -d
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openlit/openlit/main/cli/scripts/install.sh | sh
openlit configure --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:4318
openlit coding install --vendor=claude-code
openlit coding install --vendor=codex
openlit doctor

basis.shows: Documents OpenTelemetry-native tracing, a coding-agent session dashboard, and explicit installation commands for Claude Code and Codex instrumentation. The documented captured data includes prompts, LLM calls, tool calls, sub-agent activity, token usage and costs. Apache-2.0 licensing is information only.

The local deployment has two services, OpenLIT and ClickHouse, persistent named volumes, an inspection UI on port 3000, and OTLP receivers on ports 4317 and 4318. This establishes a concrete local storage path; it does not establish RAM use or ingestion speed.
The CLI suite runs go test -race -count=1 ./..., checks embedded plugin synchronization, and cross-compiles the CLI for macOS arm64.
The inspected October 1 default-branch commit has a completed SUCCESS result for the CLI Go test job; plugin synchronization also succeeded in this run.
The same inspected commit has a completed SUCCESS result for the darwin-arm64 CLI build. This is cross-compilation evidence, not a complete macOS installation test.

The server release workflow publishes Linux amd64 and arm64 images. Linux amd64 fits the WSL2 host; the arm64 image provides a documented route through Docker on Apple Silicon. GPU execution is unnecessary for the required trace-store job.

The dashboard has an upstream Jest coverage suite, type checking, linting and a container build. Its existence is supporting test evidence; a successful Jest run was not present in the sampled documentation commit's checks.

The latest GitHub release was published September 10, 2026, inside the 90-day window. Release notes report expanded dashboard tests and branch coverage above 96%; that upstream report is not a cross-repository benchmark.
The repository is not archived. Its default-branch commit 897838a26e447f7f82dccfb59f7cbe0bfba3b694 is dated October 1, 2026, and sampled issues were updated October 1–2.

not_selected.name: Opik
not_selected.reason: Strong local OpenTelemetry, LLM-tracing and evaluation alternative with self-hosted agent-accessible MCP and passing SDK/E2E checks; the consulted README gives a less explicit path for capturing both coding agents' own sessions than OpenLIT's vendor instrumentation commands. [README](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/blob/3de1c5e630ff/README.md), [E2E CI](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/actions/runs/36891099668/job/110466634676), [October 1 release](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/releases/tag/2.2.87).

not_selected.name: HyperDX / ClickStack
not_selected.reason: Good OTLP storage and inspection fit, with an all-in-one deployment, agent-friendly SQL/NDJSON CLI and passing OTLP smoke tests; its documented strengths center on general observability rather than the required coding-agent session capture, and no shared measurement establishes an advantage here. [README](https://github.com/hyperdxio/hyperdx/blob/b52adf718944/README.md), [OTLP smoke CI](https://github.com/hyperdxio/hyperdx/actions/runs/36920517517/job/110565115653), [October 1 CLI release](https://github.com/hyperdxio/hyperdx/releases/tag/cli-v0.6.4).

not_selected.name: Jaeger
not_selected.reason: Strong tracing alternative with passing unit and persistent-storage integration tests, Linux amd64/macOS arm64 release artifacts, and recent MCP/LLM-related changes; its documented quickstart uses in-memory storage, so persistent local retention requires additional configuration, while OpenLIT more directly documents both coding-agent integrations. [README](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/e95545457675/README.md), [Badger integration CI](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/actions/runs/36954903126/job/110675620846), [September 14 release](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/releases/tag/v2.21.0).

not_selected.name: Langfuse
not_selected.reason: Strong finalist for LLM/agent inspection and evaluations, with passing ingestion/UI-related suites; its supported local deployment contains six services, versus OpenLIT's two, and the inspected sources do not establish better ingestion or inspection of both named clients. The service-count comparison concerns installation complexity, not measured resource use. [Compose](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/9a29212e855c/docker-compose.yml), [CI](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/actions/runs/36876004364/job/110415490324), [October 1 release](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/releases/tag/v4.49.0).

not_selected.name: LangWatch
not_selected.reason: Closest coding-agent challenger: documents Claude Code/Codex wrappers and npx @langwatch/server, but that command provisions a multi-component stack, and sampled recent Linux package-smoke checks contain both successes and failures; this leaves clean-install reliability unresolved and does not prove platform inability. [README](https://github.com/langwatch/langwatch/blob/83d152e18926/README.md), [packaged-server test](https://github.com/langwatch/langwatch/blob/83d152e18926/.github/workflows/npx-server-smoke.yml), [failed Ubuntu check](https://github.com/langwatch/langwatch/actions/runs/36943823560/job/110641200464), [successful Ubuntu check](https://github.com/langwatch/langwatch/actions/runs/36943906666/job/110641460638).

not_selected.name: MLflow
not_selected.reason: Strong finalist with a simple uvx mlflow server path, OpenTelemetry tracing, experiment tracking and upstream tracing benchmarks; the README's agent-assisted setup instruments application code, while complete capture of the named Codex sessions was not verified in this review. Its tracking overlap could reverse the choice in the deciding comparison. [README](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/5fb75a55ed41/README.md), [tracing benchmark workflow](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/5fb75a55ed41/.github/workflows/tracing-benchmark.yml), [September 17 release](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/releases/tag/v3.16.1).

not_selected.name: OpenObserve
not_selected.reason: Credible local single-binary/Docker OpenTelemetry store with LLM observability and passing database/UI checks; the inspected sources provide less direct evidence for capturing both coding-agent sessions, and its advertised Elasticsearch storage comparison does not measure this layer's workload. [README](https://github.com/openobserve/openobserve/blob/3e15abc94719/README.md), [database CI](https://github.com/openobserve/openobserve/actions/runs/36936983395/job/110619642062), [September 30 release](https://github.com/openobserve/openobserve/releases/tag/v1.1.0-rc1).

not_selected.name: SigNoz
not_selected.reason: Capable self-hosted OpenTelemetry/LLM inspection platform with MCP access, passing Go tests and Linux amd64/macOS arm64 release artifacts; no inspected measurement establishes a better fit for the two coding-agent sessions or a distinct job requiring it alongside the provisional choice. Optional cloud-only Noz is not needed for the required trace-store capability. [README](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz/blob/1643df620bbe/README.md), [Go CI](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz/actions/runs/36921838943/job/110569529369), [September 29 release](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz/releases/tag/v0.144.0).

excluded.name: Uptrace
excluded.fact: As of October 2, 2026 UTC, the latest default-branch commit returned by the GitHub commits API is f617f6c76a035a1b2a83cc19cb2bc2802a68f0a6, dated June 14, 2026, outside the frozen 90-day window. The repository is not archived, but its August 13 pushed_at timestamp does not establish a newer default-branch commit. [Default-branch commits API](https://api.github.com/repos/uptrace/uptrace/commits?per_page=1), [commit](https://github.com/uptrace/uptrace/commit/f617f6c76a03).

layers.deciding_comparison: No unique measured winner is established. OpenLIT is the provisional fit choice because its documented installation covers persistent local OTLP storage and both named coding-agent integrations with two deployment services. Currency does not separate the nine non-stale candidates: all are unarchived, have October 1–2 default-branch commits, releases inside 90 days, and sampled October 1–2 issue activity. The primary head-to-head is OpenLIT versus LangWatch on a fresh WSL2 Ubuntu x86_64 host; include MLflow to resolve experiment-tracking overlap, with Langfuse and Jaeger as additional strong finalists if practical. Feed identical fixed OTLP fixtures and actual Claude Code/Codex sessions through each supported integration. First require complete ingestion, correct session/parent relationships, preservation of LLM/tool attributes and persistence across restart. Then compare a fixed inspection/query task set, installation effort, dropped spans, ingestion delay, p50/p95 query latency, idle/peak RAM and CPU, and disk growth. Assess whether experiment tracking adds a needed job or duplicates work. Repeat installation and the correctness checks on macOS arm64. The RTX 4090 is not required for this comparison.
evidence_gaps: The packet contains no comparison where every named arm ran. Upstream tests and CI establish exercised code paths; they do not establish comparative ingestion completeness, inspection quality or resource use on the target hosts.

ctx_fetch_and_index was blocked with: "MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never". Public README, Compose, workflow, issue and CI evidence was instead obtained through the GitHub API, indexed with ctx_index and read with ctx_search. Linked external documentation and benchmark pages were not fetched through the requested route.

OpenLIT's current README and CI were inspected at commit 897838a26e447f7f82dccfb59f7cbe0bfba3b694. Its documented quickstart uses a floating server image and a main-branch CLI installer; a matching immutable server/CLI release bundle and complete cold installation were not verified.

OpenLIT's Python provider test job is commented out because it requires live service credentials; the successful CLI, TypeScript and build checks must not be generalized to all provider integrations. Source: https://github.com/openlit/openlit/blob/897838a26e44/.github/workflows/ci-python.yml.
Linux amd64 build/test evidence and macOS arm64 cross-compilation support the platform assessment, but complete WSL2 and Apple Silicon deployments were not exercised.

CI snapshots cover the three latest commits per non-stale repository, with at most 100 check contexts per commit. They are samples, not historical pass-rate measurements. LangWatch has mixed Linux smoke results; Jaeger's sampled tracing tests passed despite separate Scorecard and Metrics Comparison failures.

Agent integration commands in upstream READMEs do not themselves prove that every native telemetry signal becomes a complete trace. The deciding comparison must distinguish OTLP traces from logs/metrics and check any supported adapters or hooks.

Budget used: 30 GitHub API requests, including one GraphQL request for source/test/CI/issue data; one denied fetch batch requesting four pages; two web-search queries that supplied no usable evidence.
